answer: A reputation bond makes Sybil attacks expensive: before an agent can trade, it must lock a stake that grows with its transaction volume, and the stake is slashed if peers report fraud. A newcomer starts at the foot of a trust summit, and climbing it requires verified, paid work over time, so each fake identity needs its own funded climb. The delta between a bonded agent's earnings and the cost of forging a new identity stays positive only for honest actors, and every stake and slash is recorded in a crystal-clear public ledger anyone can audit.
